narrative: Material PL1__MF5A8C08 exhibits smooth, normally distributed daily demand averaging 10,654 units (CV=14.3%) with no detectable trend over the 130-day observation window. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=45.9%, mean 2.39 days), with transport variance being the dominant uncertainty driver. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended, anchored on an EOQ of 111,681 units that consolidates ~779 annual replenishments into ~24, reducing total inventory costs by 92.8% while introducing a 19,555-unit safety stock to protect the 95% service level target.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and approximately normal (CV=14.3%); the (r,Q) model is optimal for this pattern as it directly balances ordering and holding costs via EOQ and uses the compound lead-time-demand standard deviation for the safety stock, making it tractable and auditable in SAP.
research_insights.boundary_risk: EOQ of 111,681 units sits comfortably within the 149,768-unit storage limit (utilisation 87.6%). No capacity cap was applied. If storage shrinks or safety stock rises, the cap could bind and reduce EOQ headroom.
